idiom_name: if (!ok) return; early-return guards, with assert for programmer-error preconditions
implementation_notes: C++ realises the guard as a plain if with an early return or throw, and RAII is what makes it cheap: the destructors of everything constructed before the guard run on the exit path, so the pattern no longer needs a single-exit discipline and the goto-chain case disappears. For conditions that indicate programmer error rather than bad input, use assert (disabled when NDEBUG is defined, per cppreference) or the C++26 contract_assert statement; keep explicit guards with real exceptions for anything a caller can cause. The classic wrapped if/else is still right when the condition binds a value the happy path needs, and C++17 if-with-initializer keeps that form flat: if (auto cfg = load(); !cfg) return fallback;.
pitfalls: assert is compiled out when NDEBUG is defined, so it never guards input validation; use explicit checks that throw for anything a caller can trigger.
Throwing from a destructor or a noexcept function terminates the program; guards that throw must not sit on those paths.
Acquiring a raw resource and checking it afterwards (pointer first, owner later) reopens the leak window RAII removes; acquire into the owning type first, then test the owner.
